title: Federal enforcement actions already announced
question: Which criminal cases, settlements and penalties involving Bay Area health providers has the federal health inspector general already listed?
finding: Of 604 enforcement entries the inspector general's site returns for California and San Francisco, 52 name a Bay Area place in the title or mention San Francisco on the page (20 by title); 14 are dated 2024 or later. The most recent is dated 2026-07-23: "CEO Of Bay Area Home Health Agency Convicted Of Health Care Fraud Conspiracy Targeting Medicare".
how: The inspector general's enforcement listing, as returned by the site's own search for "California" and for "San Francisco" (the site has no State field). An entry is kept when its title names the Bay Area, one of the six counties or one of their larger cities, or when the search matched "San Francisco". Each row links to the official announcement.
limits: These are announcements by prosecutors and the inspector general. A charge or indictment is an accusation, and a settlement resolves allegations; the announcement behind each link says which it is and what, if anything, was admitted. A page can mention San Francisco only because the federal prosecutor's office there announced a case about a provider elsewhere in northern California, and a company named for its head office may have been penalized for conduct in other States. The search misses actions whose pages use neither word.
